what_this_is: Hand-written stand-ins for reasoning-tier PL/SQL conversions, used while Bedrock InvokeModel is blocked on this account. NOT model output. An entry is keyed on owner, object_type and object_name and is written against the source object's SHA-256 ('written_against'); if the live source differs, convert/model.py refuses the entry as stale and the object goes to a person. Every entry passes the same five gates the rule tier does.
why_empty: Every PL/SQL object on DBMIG_APP is inside the deterministic tier's subset (convert/constructs.json), so on this estate the model tier had nothing to do and no stand-in was needed. That is the result, not a gap. An entry belongs here only when the rules decline a real object on this estate.

entry_shape.evidence: what was checked on the source when this was written
